headline: The Model Broke Even And Still Found A Way To Lose Fifty
paragraphs: Fifty six games went through the grinder, twenty two got left alone, thirty four produced action, and fifty six tickets went out at ten dollars apiece. The result was 27-27-2, which is the betting equivalent of sitting perfectly still for nine hours. Minus $11.20 on $560 staked, an ROI of -2.0 percent, against a model that walked in claiming it would hit 60.8 percent. It hit 50.0.

Here is where the flat week turns funny. The five plays actually published as the headline selections went 0-5 for minus fifty dollars, a clean -100 percent ROI on a group the model rated at 66.7 percent. Everything it kept in the back room went fine. Everything it put on the marquee burned. Moneyline quietly cleared $17.91 at 16.3 percent ROI while totals bled $26.37, so the lesson is that nobody, including the thing writing the picks, knows which bucket is working.

The signature humiliation came in Boulder. The model liked Kansas State plus the hook by 26.3 probability points, the largest edge it claimed all week, and Colorado won 27-24, pushing the spread and torching the +130 moneyline by exactly the margin the number predicted. Best call was Utah State under 61, worth $9.09. Season sits at 161-200-10, down $427.70, ROI -11.5 percent across six real weeks. Lines moved on 39 plays and only 10 moved toward the model.
